data.title: AI TRENDS | OpenAI's Sam Altman Says AI Can Be Developed Safely
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he believes AI companies can safely develop the technology without causing major harm to the public, and that he is very confident in his company’s and the industry’s ability to do so.

data.title: OpenAI Discusses New Private Funding Round at About $1.2 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
OpenAI is discussing a new private funding round with investors at a target valuation of about $1.2 trillion as it prepares for a future IPO. According to ChainCatcher, the company’s valuation reached $852 billion after a financing round completed in March this year.

The company is also discussing additional fundraising plans with large investors, and the talks are still at an early stage. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said an IPO may not come before 2027.

data.title: Blackstone Targets $8 Billion for Green Infrastructure Credit Fund
data.description: Blackstone Inc. is seeking to raise at least $8 billion for a private credit fund focused on renewables and digital infrastructure investments, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Senate Republicans Weigh Fast-Track Bill to Curb Consumer Energy Costs
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, U.S. Senate Republicans are considering an accelerated legislative process to advance a bill before the November election aimed at curbing rising consumer energy costs, with the measure targeting energy-intensive data centers.

data.title: House Panel Votes 41-0 To Hold Leon Black In Contempt Over Epstein Probe
data.description: According to CNBC, the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee voted 41-0 on Tuesday to recommend that the full House hold former Apollo Global Management CEO Leon Black in contempt of Congress after he refused to comply with subpoenas tied to the panel's investigation of Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. Black had declined to give further testimony and to turn over multiple nondisclosure agreements, and he sued the committee on Sept. 3 in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., seeking to block enforcement of the subpoenas. Oversight Chair Rep. James Comer said subpoenas carry the force of law and that the committee had no choice but to pursue contempt. Ranking Democrat Rep. Robert Garcia said the panel should not allow Black to defy congressional subpoenas and said the investigation aims to support Epstein's survivors and drive reforms. Black's lawyers called the committee's move an abuse of power and said they had the constitutional right to sue Comer and the committee because the subpoenas were illegitimate. Black stepped down as Apollo CEO in March 2021, two months after the firm said he paid Epstein $158 million for tax and estate planning advice from 2012 through 2017.

data.title: Oaktree’s Poli Sees Yields Rising as Inflation Fears Persist
data.description:
Oaktree Portfolio Manager Danielle Poli said markets may keep facing upward pressure on yields because investors do not yet believe inflation is fully tamed, according to Bloomberg.

She made the comments in an interview with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close."

data.title: Dutch Bros CEO Targets 2,029 Shops by 2029, Adds 185 This Year
data.description:
Dutch Bros President and CEO Christine Barone said the coffee chain aims to reach 2,029 shops by 2029 and expects to add at least 185 locations this year, according to Bloomberg.

Barone said the expansion is supported by an internal talent pipeline with more than 500 operators ready to move into new states and markets as the company grows.

data.title: Commonwealth LNG Plans Expansion to Nearly Double Export Capacity
data.description:
Commonwealth LNG plans a second phase that would nearly double export capacity at its Louisiana natural gas export terminal under construction, according to Bloomberg.

The developer said the expansion comes as buyers in Asia push for more US fuel.

data.title: BIS Study Finds Bitcoin Onchain Transfer Estimates Can Vary Sixfold
data.description:
Researchers at the Bank for International Settlements found that estimates of Bitcoin onchain transfer values can differ by as much as sixfold depending on how transactions are measured. According to Cointelegraph, the finding applies to onchain Bitcoin transfer values rather than trading volume on crypto exchanges, and the gap comes from differences in measurement methods, including how change outputs and transfers back to the sender are treated. The researchers said Bitcoin’s transaction structure creates the discrepancy because unspent funds are often returned to the sender as change, which can appear as another output even when no funds are being transferred to another party. They also wrote that metrics such as transaction volumes, market capitalisation and total value locked can suggest a level of accuracy that is not supported by the underlying data. The study, based on 100 billion blockchain records across Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron, found that similar measurement issues extend across the broader crypto ecosystem.

The researchers also said the measurement problem affects Bitcoin’s market capitalization, with the conventional measure at times as much as four times higher than realized capitalization, which values each coin at the price when it last moved. According to Cointelegraph, Ethereum presented a separate challenge because of the spread of smart contracts, with about 54 million of roughly 67.5 million active contracts examined unable to be categorized using the study’s classifications. Stablecoin activity also proved difficult to interpret because the same asset can serve different purposes across blockchains. The researchers said USDT on Ethereum was more closely linked to DeFi activity, while USDT on Tron was associated more with payment-like and store-of-value purposes. They added that the share of USDT held by smart contracts on Ethereum exceeded 20% in 2022, compared with around 1% on Tron. Because of those differences, the researchers said aggregating USDT activity across blockchains can conflate different types of economic activity and obscure how stablecoins are actually being used. They concluded that onchain indicators should be treated as noisy approximations rather than direct measures of economic activity. Visa already separates raw and adjusted stablecoin data on its Onchain Analytics dashboard, which is powered by data from Allium Labs. Visa said its adjusted methodology is designed to remove distortions from high-frequency trading, bots, bridge routing and internal exchange operations. The dashboard currently shows $6.4 trillion in total stablecoin transaction volume across the networks it tracks over the past 30 days, compared with $313.1 billion in adjusted volume.

data.title: Wintermute Cuts Short Exposure After CLARITY Act Fails to Advance
data.description: Onchain Lens said Wintermute began taking profits on its short positions after the CLARITY Act failed to advance. According to Odaily, Wintermute's short exposure fell from $102.1 million to $55.54 million, while unrealized profit rose from $928,000 to $2.28 million. Its ETH short position also dropped from 15,330 ETH to 7,810 ETH, and cumulative profit reached $179.89 million.

data.title: Stephen Harper Says Canada Previously Had to Withdraw From U.S. Trade Talks
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, former Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper said Canada previously had to withdraw from trade talks with the United States.

data.title: Rick Pitcairn Cautions Wealthy Clients on SpaceX, Private Markets
data.description:
Rick Pitcairn, chairman and chief global strategist at family office Pitcairn, said it is his job to tap the brakes on wealthy clients who want to put too much money into "shiny star" investments such as SpaceX or private markets, according to Bloomberg.

He said private credit and private markets have a role, but they should be part of a diversified portfolio.

data.title: STOCKS | Baltic Exchange Data Shows Record $44.8 Million Cost to Ship U.S. Gulf Crude to Asia
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Baltic Exchange data showed that as of Tuesday, the cost of chartering a very large crude carrier to transport 2 million barrels of U.S. Gulf crude to Asia was about $44.8 million, a record high.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Spot Gold Falls 0.16% in New York Late Trading
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, spot gold fell 0.16% to $4,292.85 per ounce in New York late trading on Tuesday, September 15, while spot silver rose 0.70% to $63.6661 per ounce and COMEX copper futures gained 0.80% to $6.4545 per pound. The Philadelphia Gold and Silver Index, traded during U.S. stock market hours, closed up 0.01% at 387.64, the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index fell 0.53% to 2,693.03, and the Materials Index rose 0.37% while the Metals and Mining Index gained 0.14%.

data.title: U.S. Presses Mexico to Accept New AI Hardware Export Rules
data.description:
The U.S. government is pressuring Mexican officials to accept new rules on artificial intelligence hardware exports, according to people familiar with the matter. According to ChainCatcher, trade officials from the two countries are expected to hold another round of talks in Washington as early as next week.

The discussions are also expected to cover the possibility of lowering U.S. tariffs on steel, aluminum, and automobiles.

data.title: Crypto Transactions on Agentic Payment Rails Are Surging
data.description:
Crypto transactions on agentic payment rails are surging. According to Bloomberg, the increase is being driven by AI agents that can make payments on behalf of users.

The article says these rails are designed to let software agents handle transactions, and that activity on them has risen. It also says the trend is tied to the growing use of AI agents in payments.

data.title: AI | Anthropic Expands Finance Ties With BlackRock
data.description:
BlackRock senior managing director Jaime Magyera said advisers are using artificial intelligence to help parse increasingly complex capital markets after Anthropic announced new ties with BlackRock, according to Bloomberg.

Magyera also said AI is helping create more strategic customization for clients.

data.title: ExxonMobil Gets Texas Approval for Rose Carbon-Capture Project
data.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. won approval for its Rose carbon-capture project in Texas in a 2-to-1 vote, according to Bloomberg. The decision allows ExxonMobil to move ahead with the emission-reducing development, which could be among the biggest of its kind.

data.title: Bond Traders Bet Fed Will Extend Treasury Selloff
data.description:
Bond traders have built extreme short positions ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, betting the Treasury selloff will continue, according to Bloomberg.

The move comes as yields have climbed to their highest levels in more than a decade.

data.title: STOCKS | Mortgage Insurers Fall After FHFA Chief Bill Pulte Hints at Fee Relief
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, mortgage insurance stocks fell after FHFA Director Bill Pulte suggested that homeowners should not be forced to pay mortgage insurance fees in some cases, with MGIC Investment Corp. down 3.1% for its worst single-day performance since April, Essent Group Ltd. down 0.9%, and Radian Group Inc. and NMI Holdings Inc. both down 1.4%.
